Revised assessment incorporating economics/finance literature:
- The statement’s tone is net negative due to clear downside risks to growth and disinflation pressures, but it is partially offset by aggressive policy easing consistent with evidence on credit channels and expectations management.
- Supporting sentences:
  • “The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook.”
  • “Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined…”
  • “The Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 0 to 1/4 percent.”
  • “Over coming months the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $500 billion and … agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $200 billion.”
  • “The Federal Reserve is prepared to use its full range of tools to support the flow of credit…,” including expanded repos, a lower primary credit rate, and coordinated U.S. dollar swap lines.

Literature-based rationale for adjustment:
- Credit and bank-lending channels: Easing via QE, discount window, and repo operations helps offset adverse shocks by reducing external finance premia and supporting investment and spending (Bernanke–Gertler financial accelerator; Gertler and Gilchrist (1994); Oliner and Rudebusch (1996a); Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein (1994)).
- Liquidity trap/ZLB: With policy rates at the effective lower bound and declining inflation compensation, asset purchases and forward guidance are appropriate tools to prevent deflationary spirals (liquidity trap references; Svensson (1997a); Svensson and Woodford (1999) on expectations/forecast targeting).
- International dollar funding stress: Swap lines with other central banks mitigate global financial conditions and support credit markets, consistent with the “credit view” that alleviating funding frictions stabilizes real activity.
- Net effect: While the growth/inflation outlook is clearly deteriorating (negative), the literature suggests these tools materially cushion the downturn, warranting a slightly less negative score than the initial -0.60.
